4.text: The artificial “spell” may appear in various shapes, and also may change

5.text: its appearance at the will of its creator. Often it is an animal, or even a

6.text: group of animals, or, on the contrary, only some part of the carcass, — for

7.text: instance, the upper half of a ground-seal, a fox-head without body or legs, —

8.text: also a man or a woman, or even any inanimate object, such as a stone or a tree.

9.text: In some cases the first sight of the materialized “spell” makes the victim

10.text: lose his reason, and die raving mad. In other cases, on the contrary, the

11.text: victim believes that he has before himself a real animal, a fit object for hunt;

12.text: and the ultimate catastrophe happens quite naturally as an accident of the

13.text: hunt. Thus I obtained a very characteristic story about two Chukchee families

14.text: between whom an old feud existed. At last one family left the country, and

15.text: settled at a distance of several hundred miles. After a number of years, a

16.text: wild reindeer-buck came to the camp of one of the members of this family,

17.text: and began to graze in sight of the houses. Of course, it was only a materi-

18.text: alized “spell,” because a real reindeer would not dare to come so near a human

19.text: habitation. It was sent by the “knowing people” of the other family, who had

20.text: not forgotten that the last bloodshed was effected by their adversaries.

21.text: The time was well chosen, because, of all the men of the camp, only

22.text: the master was present. On seeing the reindeer, he shot at it with his bow.

23.text: The reindeer took to flight, but ran rather slowly, being evidently wounded

24.text: by the arrow. The man, who was fleet of foot, followed in pursuit. This

25.text: was the last time he was seen alive by any person. After two days, his

26.text: wife, alarmed by his prolonged absence, went to a neighboring camp several

27.text: miles distant, and asked the people to help her in her hunt for the missing

28.text: man. After a few hours’ search, they found him on a large lake in the

29.text: vicinity. It was early in the fall, and the ice of the lake was not yet covered

30.text: with snow. The fleeing reindeer had lured him upon the ice, and there in

31.text: a swift chase the man fell down and broke his neck. Of course, no trace

32.text: of the reindeer was to be seen. It had fulfilled its mission, and without doubt

33.text: had returned to the “knowing people” who had sent it on its errand. I had

34.text: this story from the brother of the man who perished, and his death was scored

35.text: up as a new case for revenge against the other party.¹

36.text: In a Chukchee tale, several versions of which were collected, a man or

37.text: a woman desiring to have revenge on a female foe creates a dog of snow,

38.text: of brindle-wolf color, and transforms it into a young man. The “spell” is

39.text: immediately sent to the camp of the victim, where it acts like a real young

40.text: man, and succeeds in making love to the woman “doomed to anger.” The
